record.original_question: Randomized SVD: Let (A R^n x d ) be a matrix, fix $r > 0$, and let (Omega R^n x k ) be an oblivious subspace injection with dimension $r$ and injectivity (1-epsilon ). Let $~A = (AOmega)(AOmega)^+A$ denote the randomized SVD approximation to $A$, and let $A_r$ be the best rank-$r$ approximation to $A$ with respect to the Frobenius norm. Prove or disprove: Does it necessarily hold that [ |A - ~A |_ F <= (1+O(epsilon)) |A-A_r |_ F? ]

evidence.quote: Let \(A \in \mathbb R^{n \times d}\) be a matrix, fix $r > 0$, and let \(\Omega \in \mathbb R^{n \times k}\) be an oblivious subspace injection with dimension $r$ and injectivity \(1-\varepsilon\). Let $\tilde{A} = (A\Omega)(A\Omega)^+A$ denote the randomized SVD approximation to $A$, and let $A_r$ be the best rank-$r$ approximation to $A$ with respect to the Frobenius norm. Prove or disprove: Does it necessarily hold that \[ \|A - \tilde{A}\|_{\rm F} \leq (1+\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)) \|A-A_r\|_{\rm F}? \]

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n	imes d}$ and fix an integer $r>0$. For $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, call a (random) matrix $\Omega\in\mathbb{R}^{n	imes k}$ an oblivious subspace injection of dimension $r$ with injectivity $1-\varepsilon$ if, for every fixed $r$-dimensional subspace $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n}$, with high probability the map $x\mapsto \Omega^{	op}x$ restricted to $V$ satisfies
$$(1-\varepsilon)\|x\|_2^2\le \|\Omega^{	op}x\|_2^2\le(1+\varepsilon)\|x\|_2^2\qquad	ext{for all }x\in V.$$
Define the randomized SVD approximation
$$	ilde A \;=\; (A\Omega)(A\Omega)^{+}A,$$
where $(\cdot)^{+}$ denotes the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse, and let $A_r$ be a best rank-$r$ approximation to $A$ in the Frobenius norm, i.e. a minimizer of $\|A-B\|_F$ over all matrices $B$ of rank at most $r$.

Prove or disprove: there is an absolute constant $C>0$ (independent of $A$, $r$, $n$, $d$, $k$) such that
$$\|A-	ilde A\|_F \;\le\; (1+C\varepsilon)\,\|A-A_r\|_F.$$
artifact.status_search_result: This is the standard guarantee for sketch-based randomized low-rank approximation. Sarlós (2006) and the analyses of subspace-embedding-based randomized SVD (e.g., Clarkson–Woodruff, Halko–Martinsson–Tropp, Woodruff's survey "Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra") establish that if $\Omega$ is an oblivious subspace embedding for $r$-dimensional subspaces with distortion $\varepsilon$, then $\|A-(A\Omega)(A\Omega)^+A\|_F \le (1+O(\varepsilon))\|A-A_r\|_F$. The statement is therefore known to be true.

status_evidence.title: Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra (Woodruff)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides the (1+epsilon) Frobenius-norm low-rank approximation guarantee for sketches that are subspace embeddings, including the bound for (A\Omega)(A\Omega)^+ A.
status_evidence.claim: Standard textbook result: oblivious subspace embeddings yield (1+O(epsilon)) Frobenius low-rank approximation.

status_evidence.title: Sarlós, Improved Approximation Algorithms for Large Matrices via Random Projections
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes that random projections satisfying a subspace embedding property give relative-error Frobenius low-rank approximations.
status_evidence.claim: Original source for the (1+epsilon) Frobenius bound for projection-based randomized low-rank approximation.
